key_insight: TEMPO-BP improves quantum LDPC decoding by adapting each variable’s memory strength through local feedback from the evolving decoding state.
engineering_relevance: More reliable decoding with shallow concurrent runs could help realize qLDPC codes’ potential to reduce fault-tolerant quantum computing overhead.
method: Use state-dependent local feedback to control memory strength in belief propagation.
Run ensembles of 10–15 concurrent decoder instances with reduced per-instance iteration caps.
Assess memory control through ablations and characterize amplification modes with loop-gain analysis.
evidence_signal: On the gross code at 0.4% physical error, single-run TEMPO-BP achieved 0.73% per-shot logical failure versus 2.51% for BP+OSD+CS-10; ensembles matched or lowered Relay-BP-5 failure counts at all ten tested operating points with at least tenfold lower per-instance iteration caps.
watch_item: Lower iteration caps do not alone establish lower hardware latency or total resource cost, particularly when running concurrent ensembles.
paper_title: Closing the loop on memory: accurate, shallow and transferable decoding of quantum LDPC codes
